chapter_title: Concerning the Ad[vent] of the Apostle
chapter_note: This chapter is entirely institutional/apostolic narrative with no extractable substrate. Teaching purity is near zero (0.018). The chapter traces apostolic succession from Sethel through Jesus to Mani, recounts Mani's autobiography (calling, revelation by the Paraclete, missionary journeys), and frames his apostolate as the fulfillment of Jesus's Paraclete promise. The agricultural metaphor (farmer/harvest/Parmuthi-Paophi) maps apostles→farmers and churches→harvest seasons — both sides of the mapping are institutional/worldly, not cosmological. Cosmological content appears only as referenced topics in the revelation summary (¶24-25: 'the mystery of the light and the darkness,' ships, Adam) but is never actually taught — it functions as a table of contents for cosmological teachings given elsewhere. NT citations (Phil. 2:7 servant's form, John 14-16 Paraclete passages) confirm the editorial period. The chapter is bookended by dialogue frame conventions (opening question ¶1-2, formulaic closing ¶31). This is a foundational institutional text for the Manichaean community, establishing Mani's legitimacy through apostolic succession.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Opening question about Mani's apostolate, journeying, and church-choosing. Structurally a dialogue frame opening, but the question content is entirely institutional (apostolate, cities, church) — not a cosmological question. High dialogue_frame (11.9) and institutional (21.43) scores.
Pure formulaic response: 'The apostle says to them: I [...] but I will recount to you [...]'. Highest dialogue_frame score in the chapter (28.57). No cosmological content.

Opens with exhortation address 'Understand, O my beloved ones' (exhortation score 5.68) then presents the apostolic succession analogy: apostles=farmers, churches=Parmuthi/Paophi (Egyptian harvest months). The mapping is institutional→agricultural, NOT cosmos→cosmos. No substrate present. The Coptic month names (Parmuthi, Paophi) anchor this to Egyptian editorial context.

Extended farming parable (sowing, harvesting, gardener tending fruit trees) serving the apostolic succession analogy. Zero scores across all categories. Purely illustrative material within the institutional narrative.

Application of farming analogy to apostles. Key institutional markers: 'the elect and the catechumens' (institutional score 10.17), 'the whole created order,' 'choose a selection.' Heavily lacunose but institutional intent clear.

Fragmentary. Institutional vocabulary: 'the form of his church free,' 'of the flesh, whose forms he had made free.' Institutional score 13.51. Describes the apostolic mechanism of freeing spiritual forms.
Return to farming analogy (Parmuthi, Paophi). Continues the institutional harvest metaphor. All register scores zero — pure illustrative material.

'Again, this too is [how] the apostles...' — continuation of apostolic cycle teaching. 'From the beginning of the moulding of humanity' references cosmogony but only as a temporal marker within the institutional narrative.

Detailed description of the apostolic cycle mechanism: the apostle comes down, dwells in the world, is raised up, leaves his church, becomes guardian and helper for those remaining. High institutional score (11.17). 'Land of glory' is a cosmological term but functions as a destination within institutional narrative.
Double simile: farmer glad at harvest, merchant returning with doubled cargo. Illustrative material serving the institutional teaching about apostolic completion. All register scores zero.

Extended tree/fruit analogy for continuous apostolic succession: 'There is not any time the tree is bare of fruit!' Key theological point: the world is never without the means of salvation. The tree metaphor and Parmuthi/Paophi cycle serve institutional ecclesiology. Low institutional score (3.12) but content is clearly institutional.

Explicit statement of apostolic succession mechanism: 'when the apostle will be raised up... at that instant another apostle shall be sent.' Highest institutional score yet (19.32). 'As I have told you' is a dialogue-frame self-reference within institutional narrative. 'Releases his church and saves it from the flesh [of sin]' — institutional soteriology.

The chain of apostles: Sethel → Enosh/Enoch → Sem → Buddha/Aurentes (east) → Zarathustra (Persia/Hystaspes) → Jesus. Dense historical proper nouns. Institutional score 17.82. This is the apostolic succession list — a distinctive Manichaean institutional teaching. The inclusion of Buddha and Zarathustra reflects Mani's universalist claim.

Jesus narrative with docetic christology: 'He came without body!' References Phil. 2:7 ('servant's form, an appearance as of men'). Historical details: twelve, seventy-two, sect of the Jews, Judas Iscariot. Satan/Judas narrative. This is NT-derived institutional narrative. Dialogue_frame score 2.13 from 'as I have told you about him.'

Passion/resurrection/ascension narrative: crucifixion, three-day burial, resurrection, appearance to disciples, breathing the Holy Spirit, sending them to preach, ascending. Entirely derived from Gospel accounts. All register scores zero but content is thoroughly institutional.
Fragmentary. Jesus's twelve apostles, 'raised up and rested in the greatness.' Continuation of institutional narrative about the post-ascension church.
Paul narrative: reinforced the apostles, preached, gave power. 'The church of the saviour.' Institutional score 4.08. Part of the apostolic succession from Jesus through Paul.

Decline after Paul: 'all mankind began to stumble.' Gospel allusion to narrow vs. broad road (Matt 7:13-14): 'the path which is narrow and sticky... the road which is broad.' Institutional narrative of church decline. All register scores zero.

A 'righteous man of truth' in the 'last church' — identity debated (Elchasai? Marcion? Bardaisan?). Institutional markers: 'church of our master,' 'land of light' (as destination). Then: 'the church perished. The world remained behind without church.' Institutional score 13.11. Substrate score 3.28 likely from 'land of light' — but this is cosmological vocabulary used within institutional narrative, not substrate teaching.
Brief simile for the church's perishing: tree plucked, fruits taken, remains without fruit. Illustrative material within institutional narrative. All scores zero.

Mani's apostolate begins. Direct NT citation: 'Just like the saviour said: When I go, I will send to you the Paraclete' (John 14:16/16:7). 'The Paraclete, the Spirit of truth' — Johannine language. 'This last generation' — eschatological institutional framing. Highest institutional score in chapter (31.58).

Continued Paraclete description, closely paraphrasing John 16:8-14: 'he can upbraid the world concerning sin... speak with you on behalf of righteousness, and about judgement.' Institutional score 6.56. Entirely NT-derived institutional narrative.

Fragmentary. Paraclete preaching, 'from Jesus until now' — institutional timeline. Return of harvest metaphor: 'like the month of Parmuthi that cereal shall ripen in.' Institutional score 8.22. The harvest metaphor is re-applied to the cosmic redemption of souls — but within institutional framing.

Mani's autobiography: born under Artabanus, grew under Ardashir, Paraclete descended in Ardashir's coronation year. Then a revelation summary: 'the mystery of the light and the darkness; the mystery of the calamity of conflict, and the war... through their mingling this universe was set up.' The cosmological content (light/darkness, conflict, mingling) is REFERENCED as revelation topics but NOT TAUGHT as substrate. The frame 'He unveiled to me the mystery of...' is institutional autobiography. Both sides of the revelation list stay within summary mode — this is a table of contents, not cosmological teaching.

Continuation of revelation list. Cosmological topics referenced: ships, gods of light, purification, dregs/effluent/abyss, Adam, tree of knowledge. Then explicitly institutional: 'The mystery of the elect, [with their] commandments. The mystery of the catechumens their helpers, with [their] commandments. The mystery of the sinners with their deeds.' Seam flag correctly identifies institutional vocabulary. The entire paragraph is a revelation TABLE OF CONTENTS, not substrate teaching. Substrate score 1.65 from cosmological references, but these are mentioned, not taught.

Climax of revelation claim: 'everything the eye shall see, and the ear hear' (cf. 1 Cor 2:9). Twin motif: 'I have become a single body, with a single Spirit!' Institutional autobiography — Mani's identity claim. All register scores zero except institutional (6.9).
Missionary journey: India, 'hope of life,' 'good election.' Historical proper nouns (Ardashir). Institutional score 18.92. Pure apostolic autobiography.

Dense autobiography with historical names: Ardashir, Shapur, India, Persia, Babylon, Mesene, Susiana, Parthia, Adiabene, Romans. Missionary itinerary. Institutional score 12.96. This is the most historically specific paragraph in the chapter.

Direct address to community: '[I have chosen] you, the good election, the holy church.' Missionary superiority claim: 'Not one among the apostles did ever do these things.' Eschatological promise: church will 'remain in the world until Jesus.' References to 'right side' / 'left' may echo cosmological categories but function as ecclesiological terms here. Institutional score 7.5.

Transitional summary wrapping up the narrative. Dialogue frame elements: 'about which you questioned me,' 'Today you have again questioned me.' Self-reference to 'my books already.' 'I have repeated the lesson to you in brief' — meta-commentary on the teaching session. Functions as transition to the closing frame.

Formulaic closing: disciples hear, rejoice, are enlightened, thank the master. 'We have also believed that you are the Paraclete, this one from the Father, the unveiler of all these hidden things!' — confession formula. Seam flag correctly identifies this as editorial closure. Dialogue_frame score 6.06. Chapter-level analysis notes 'formulaic closing.' Third-person narrative voice ('Then, when his disciples heard') shifts to direct speech ('We thank you, our master') — classic dialogue frame closure pattern.
